body:
I am trying to relate step1 to straightline, so as to be able to step just a few instructions at a time -- namely, those instructions that are found at a given address.

Right now, this prevents us from stepping through enough instructions that we can do some loop-based reasoning. In short, restoring `p3` from the Examples directory.

This would also be useful for #137 which, as far as I can tell, does not use `kstep`.

I did some digging and found some issues with the layout -- these were fixed in my previous PR #136. I also rephrased directivesAtAddress and directivesFromAddress to make it obvious that the former is a prefix of the latter.

Sketching the proof, it turns out we need a monotonicity lemma for Directives.interp -- this is courtesy of Gemini.

The final step is still missing, hence why this PR is still draft.

body:
The baseline theory necessary to define a notion of weakest precondition that bridges to `Std.WP` and thus `vcgen`.

* The weakest precondition of a `Program` fragment `p` is defined in terms of an ambient laid out `Host` executable. Specifically, the weakest precondition of `p` proves a statement about `Eventually (step1 Host.exe) s post` for a start state `s` of an occurrence of `p` and a postcondition `post` that holds at fallthrough or exit points of `p`.
* `Program.wp [Host] p Q E s` is the formal definition of this notion of WP.
* `Program.step1_of_wp` is the soundness bridge that eliminates a `Program.wp`-proved fact into the existing `Eventually (step1 ...)` framework.

Later PRs will demonstrate that very few (directive) specs need to make syntactic assumptions about the `Host` they are embedded in, so that layout/linking decisions are properly abstracted as much as possible. Sneak peek of #166:

```lean
theorem alu_mem_example_correct [Host] (hp : alu_mem_example.IsInfix Host.prog) (s₀ : MachineData)
    (v : UInt64) (R : DataMem → Prop)
    (h_mem : s₀.dmem =⋆ Eq (v.At (s₀.regs.rdx.toBitVec + 136#64)) ⋆ R) :
    Eventually (step1 Host.exe) (fun s' => s'.1.regs.rcx = 142) (s₀, startAddr hp) := by
  have hload := Mem.loadInt_sep _ _ 8 _ _ h_mem (UInt64.toBytes_length v) (by decide)
  apply Program.WP.step1_of_wp hp
  kvcgen64 [alu_mem_example] with finish
```

  **Generated content.** I used Claude Code to generate all Lean code in this PR. I reviewed every definition and the statements of the top-level theorems (`Program.wp`, `Host`, `Directive.Inert`, `Program.step1_of_wp`, `Program.wp_cons`, `Program.wp_mono`). I did not review the proofs line by line. I wrote all comments and docstrings myself.

body:
This PR uses the `Program.wp` definition from #165 to enable `vcgen` support via a wrapper macro `kvcgen64`. This support is opt-in via `open Program.WP`, in anticipation of other, compatible and more abstract WP definitions that bake in the frame rule. Example proof:

```lean
theorem swap_correct [layout : Layout] [Kraken.Executable.Assembled (layout swap)] (d : MachineData) :
    Eventually (straightlineStep (layout swap))
      (fun s' =>
          s'.1.regs.get Reg.rax = d.regs.get Reg.rbx ∧
          s'.1.regs.get Reg.rbx = d.regs.get Reg.rax)
      (d, layout.start) := by
  apply Program.WP.straightline_of_wp
  kvcgen64 [swap] with finish
```

Payload of this patch:

* scoped `WP` instance for `Program` and single `Directive`s + adequacy `Program.WP.straightline_of_wp`
* spec theorems for `List.nil`, `List.cons` and a couple of directives to enable some baseline examples
* `kvcgen64` macro in order not to have to specify `simplifying_assumptions` sets at use sites (yes, a workaround for a missing `vcgen` feature until I know what that feature is, precisely)
* `grind` theory for memory facts

body:
Proves the baseline's `alu_mem_example_correct` through `vcgen`, on a separation-logic weakest precondition layered over the existing semantics. Stacks on #160.

```lean
theorem Sep.alu_mem_correct (v : UInt64) :
    ⦃ fun r _ _ => v.AtM (r.rdx.toBitVec + 136#64) ⦄
      alu_mem_example
    ⦃ fun _ r _ _ => ⌜r.rcx = 142⌝ ⊓ (Int.toBytes 8 42).AtM (r.rdx.toBitVec + 136#64) ⦄ := by
  kvcgen64 [alu_mem_example] with finish
```

`Sep.alu_mem_example_correct` restates the baseline theorem verbatim and follows from this triple, for any layout.

- **Assertions** (`MProp.lean`): predicates over memory with separating conjunction; registers and flags stay state-passing.
- **Semantics** (`SepWP.lean`): `Program.run` states what a fragment does inside any burst of the baseline interpreter. `Program.run_straightlineStep` reads the run of a program back as `straightlineStep`. The WP instance is the frame closure of the run, so every triple carries the frame rule.
- **Specs** (`SepSpecs.lean`, `SepFrameProc.lean`): one triple per instruction form, chained by `vcgen`. The frame inference frames `emp` for now.
- **Registers** (`X64/Registers.lean`): `kvcgen64` folds the register state as `vcgen` steps, so long blocks stay cheap.

Next: frame inference over `ecancel`, for programs that own more memory than one instruction touches.
